why: Window maximum with a monotonic deque: keep the indices of the window in a deque whose values decrease from front to back. A new value pops every smaller value from the back (they can never be a maximum again while it is in the window), the front drops out when its index leaves the window, and the front is always the window's maximum.
hints: A heap gives O(n log k). Which values in the current window can never be the maximum of any future window?
Any value with a larger value to its right inside the window: the larger one outlives it. Remove such values for good.
Deque of indices with decreasing values: pop back while nums[back] <= nums[i]; push i; pop front if it is i - k; once i >= k-1, append nums[front]. Each index is pushed and popped once: O(n).
pitfalls: Store indices, not values, so you know when the front has left the window.
Use <= when popping from the back (or <; both work, but be consistent with duplicates).
Only start emitting once the first full window is formed.
constraints:
• 1 ≤ nums.length ≤ 105
  • -104 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 104
  • 1 ≤ k ≤ nums.length
  • (Standard bounds for this exercise; the source gives none.)
